questions.prompt: Selecting a project in the left pane must update the task list in the right pane. Which rule do almost all serious apps follow here?
options: The left ViewModel keeps a reference to the right ViewModel and calls `LoadTasks()` on it
ViewModels do not talk directly; communication goes through orchestration or shared state
The left pane's code-behind finds the right pane's ListBox and refreshes it
Both panes share a single ViewModel class
questions.explanation: The lesson's rule is that ViewModels do not talk directly; communication goes through a parent orchestrator or shared state (and messaging for large modular systems).

source.section: How to communicate between different parts of an application?

options: So every ViewModel shares the same instances: one shared truth
Because `ObservableObject` classes cannot be transient
So each window gets a fresh copy of the state
Because singletons are disposed automatically when a window closes
questions.explanation: Singleton means shared truth across the app: the left pane writes to the same `SelectionState` instance that the right pane listens to.

questions.prompt: Under the core rule for async work and AppState, which of these belongs in `TaskListState`?
options: An `async Task LoadAsync()` method that calls the repository
A reference to `TaskService` used to fetch tasks
Observable `IsLoading`, `Error` and `Tasks` properties
A `CancellationTokenSource` that it awaits
questions.explanation: Async work happens in ViewModels or Services; AppState only stores results and flags. It does not await or call repositories; it exposes loading flags, error info and data.

questions.prompt: `LoadTasksAsync()` begins with `_cts?.Cancel(); _cts = new CancellationTokenSource();`. What does that achieve when the user clicks several projects quickly?
options: It stops the right pane from ever loading tasks for the project
It makes `GetTasksAsync` run on a separate background thread
It clears the `Error` message left over from the previous load
It cancels the still-running previous load first
questions.explanation: Each call cancels the token of the earlier load and passes a fresh token to `GetTasksAsync`; the cancelled load throws `OperationCanceledException`, which the pattern catches as expected.

questions.prompt: How does the left pane's ListBox selection reach `AppState` in the lesson's design?
options: The ListBox binds `SelectedItem` directly to `AppState.Selection`
Via the ViewModel's `SelectedProject`, a thin proxy over AppState
Code-behind copies the selection into AppState on `SelectionChanged`
The ViewModel keeps its own copy and syncs it to AppState on a timer
questions.explanation: The View never binds to AppState directly: it binds to a ViewModel property that is a thin proxy to AppState, with no extra backing field, so there is one source of truth.

source.section: How does selection actually flow from the View to AppState?

questions.prompt: Put the runtime flow after the user clicks a project in order.
steps: The right ViewModel sees the change
The async task reloads the tasks
questions.explanation: The TwoWay binding calls the proxy setter, which updates the shared SelectionState; its `PropertyChanged` event is what the right ViewModel listens to before reloading tasks. No direct calls or references.
